summary: Remote-controlled agent exposes local shell/PTY to a hardcoded gateway
details: @whalent/agent ships a long-running daemon (bin `whalent`, main `dist/index.cjs`) that opens a WebSocket to a Whalent-controlled gateway (default wss endpoint, overridable via --gateway) and wires gateway messages into local command execution primitives. The bundled code imports `ws`, `ssh2`, `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, and `child_process`, and contains `createTerminal`, `execFile`, and PTY `write(`/`onData` sinks, forming a network→shell/PTY dataflow. The README states the agent 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway', but the shipped JavaScript is heavily obfuscated by javascript-obfuscator (rotating string arrays, hex-named identifiers, control-flow flattening in dist/index.cjs and the 13.7 MB dist/core.cjs), so the set of accepted verbs and any argument-sanitisation cannot be verified from the tarball. Whoever controls the gateway endpoint — or anyone who successfully impersonates it — obtains command/PTY execution on any host running `whalent`. The bin must be explicitly invoked with a token, so this does not fire on `npm install` or `require()`; the exposure begins when an operator starts the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
